newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil merger activity set to swell, bankers say.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil merger activity set to swell, bankers say.

text.p: A couple of recent small U.K. oil company takeovers is likely to reignite Europe's fever for mergers and acquisitions in the energy sector, bankers sources say.
"Lots of companies are running their slide rules over potential acquisition targets. It's just a matter of time," said one investment banker.
After a spate of deals in 1996 and early 1997 several insiders had predicted corporate deals to continue unabated.

But nothing much happened here until Ramco Energy Plc last week launched its bid for JKX Oil & Gas Plc with Dana Petroleum Plc following suit on Thursday with a friendly offer for Seafield Resources Plc.
Though these deals are tiny compared with the multi-billion dollar mergers taking place in the United States, they nevertheless suggest things are on the move again in Europe.
Investment bankers say the Europoean oil scene here is just too small to generate the same flow of bids and mergers as in the United States.
But they predict several deals will roll out of the pipeline once industry executives and financial advisers return from their summer holidays.
"The fact these guys (JKX and Seafield) are going is a sign there is more to come after the August break," said another investment banker.
Insiders say the same factors that triggered last year's activity are still at play.
After years of slashing costs in response to low crude oil prices, many companies have well-filled war chests and are still seen keen to boost their oil reserves through acquisitions.
But there is also the ongoing need for restructuring in the downstream business, which continues to suffer from overcapicity and poor refining margins.
British Petroleum and Mobil merged their European downstream businesses last year, while Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Texaco Inc this year decided to join up their U.S. refining operations.
More deals like these could be on the cards, analysts say. One industry watcher, who declined to be named, suggests a U.S. refiner like Tosco Corp might be tempted to buy a European plant.
Such a deal could be the trigger to end the deadlock currently hamstringing a badly-needed pruning of the European refining overcapacity.
With its deep pockets, Shell is one of the companies most widely tipped as ready to move in either the downstream or the upstream sector.
The oil giant has an in-house merger and acquisition team which is travelling the globe for ways to spend its cash pile of about eight billion pounds.
The Anglo-Dutch group teamed up in April with Britain's minnow Cairn Energy Plc to develop interests in Bangladesh, but has as yet shown no hurry to conclude any major purchases.
But several analysts believe Shell may be ready to pounce.
"I would certainly have them fairly high up on my list of potential acquirers," said one.
